newsitem.title: CANADA: Workers at Cargill Alberta packing plant strike.
newsitem.headline: Workers at Cargill Alberta packing plant strike.

text.p: About 1,500 workers at a major Cargill Foods Ltd meat packing plant in Alberta have walked off the job in a strike that began on Thursday.

Local press reports said the workers at the plant in High River, Alberta, 30 km south of Calgary, set up picket lines after talks broke off between the company and the United Food and Commercial Workers union late on Wednesday.
The plant processes about 4,000 heads of cattle a day, making it one of Canada's largest.
UFCW members at the plant voted 94.2 percent in favor of a strike after the previous three-year contract expired in June, union business agent Wayne Covey was quoted by the Calgary Herald as saying.
Covey said hourly wages at the plant start at C$8 an hour and workers were seeking a 65 cent an hour raise.
The company had offered a 40 cent an hour wage increase over four years.
Employees were slated to vote on another Cargill offer on Sunday.
